The '''Forest Codex''' is described in source material as the earliest known written form of the [[Belcantese Language]]. It is dated to around 650 and said to have been carved or written on birch bark.

== Significance ==

The codex gives Belcantese language history a pre-medieval written anchor. Later scholars used it as evidence that Belcantese was not only an oral forest tradition but also a language of record, memory, and regional identity.

== Legacy ==

The Forest Codex became important to postwar cultural restoration because it supported claims of deep Belcantese continuity before Vesperan occupation. It was cited by language reformers and cultural historians as a symbol of survival.
